tags.chapter_name: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties

question.text: Suppose a gaseous mixture of \(\mathrm{He}, \mathrm{Ne}, \mathrm{Ar}\) and \(\mathrm{Kr}\) is treated with photons of the frequency appropriate to ionize Ar. What ion(s) will be present in the mixture?

solution.text:
Hint: \(\mathrm{He} > \mathrm{Ne} > \mathrm{Ar} > \mathrm{Kr} > \mathrm{Xe} > \mathrm{Rn}\) (Order of lonization energy)
Energy of photon is sufficient to ionize \(\mathrm{Ar}\), hence \(\mathrm{Kr}\) will also ionize.
Therefore mixture contains \(\mathrm{Ar}^{+}\)and \(\mathrm{Kr}^{+}\)
